raw_response:
*Thirty years on this land. Here's how I'm thinking about this year.*

---

My 6 mu — I keep 4 mu on wheat and maize back to back, same as always, same as my neighbors. The other 2 mu I put in stevia. The factory in Quzhou town buys it, price is better than grain. But I don't want to do too much stevia — if the factory drops the price, I still need grain to eat and sell.

**Wheat** is already in from October. I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu before I planted — 50 kg, the kind with 15-15-15 on the bag. Same as last year. My neighbor Lao Wang puts down more, but my yields are fine so I don't want to waste money. Now it's spring, the wheat is coming back up. In another few weeks at jointing I'll spread about 20 jin of urea per mu by hand — been doing it that way for 20 years. I'll water it three times: I already did the winter water, jointing water is coming, then I'll see if heading needs it. If it looks okay I'll skip the third time — pumping costs money now, they put the meter on the well two years ago. I'll spray herbicide after it comes up if I see the wild oats again like last year.

**Maize** — the real rush is getting it in fast after wheat. I'll hire the combine to cut the wheat and also chop the stalks, that saves me tillage time. Then I have maybe five or six days to get the maize seed in. I'll buy the same hybrid as last year from the seed shop — it gave me around 450 kg per mu, which was decent. I put compound fertilizer in the furrow with the seed — about 20-25 kg per mu — then come back with urea when it's knee-high, same 20 jin per mu. Usually July and August bring rains here, so I might only irrigate once, maybe twice if it's dry. The maize mostly takes care of itself if the rains come.

**Stevia** — this is the 4th year on my 2 mu, so the roots are established. I don't replant. I cut it three times: late spring, midsummer, and once more in early fall before frost. My wife and my son help with the cutting — it's all by hand, heavy work. After each cut I spread some compound fertilizer to help it grow back. I water it more than the wheat, maybe 4-5 times, because if it gets too dry the leaves go small and the factory docks the price. I need to check for bugs in summer — last year there were some aphids and I had to spray once.

The big worry is input prices went up again. I'm not changing my amounts — I'll do what I did last year. Maybe spend a bit less on the maize irrigation if it rains well.
